facts.text: Valley Grande was originally called Valley Creek in 1819 before being renamed Summerfield in 1845 to honor Methodist preacher John Summerfield.
In 1841 the Alabama Conference of the Methodist Church opened the Methodist Centenary Institute, a co‑educational school chartered by the legislature.
George Phillips planted a cotton plantation called Grand View in the area that later became Valley Grande.
The historic core of Summerfield, now part of Valley Grande, remains intact and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places covering 56.12 acres.
The first academy in Dallas County, chartered in 1829, was located in Valley Creek, the town that would become Valley Grande.
Today Valley Grande still encompasses the historic community of Summerfield, preserving its 19th‑century heritage.
